abstract: Twelve methane-sensing satellites were tested for their accuracy in measuring controlled-release events in the Arizona desert over a year-long blind test. Many were found to detect and quantify releases accurately, with instruments purpose-built for methane sensing performing best. Teams that used various methods to analyse satellite data in a methane controlled-release test achieved mostly accurate results.
title: Large blind test of methane-detecting satellites lends credibility to emissions data

abstract: Governments around the world have pledged to conserve 30% of the terrestrial realm by 2030, but official data suggest that the target is barely halfway to being met. A combined global and national-level data set now shows that up to 27% of land area is conserved, but gaps in ecological representation remain. Coverage of protected and conserved areas is higher than expected, but ecological representativeness could be improved.
title: Lay of the land: terrestrial conservation efforts cover a wider area than thought

abstract: Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells are the stem cells of the lung’s air sacs and are responsible for maintaining alveolar structure and gas exchange. A study that tracked AT2 cells shows that, after injury to the airway, they can also migrate between lung compartments and become bronchiolar cells to help repair damaged airways. Alveolar type 2 cells can migrate from the lung’s air sacs into the airways to repair damage there.
title: Alveolar stem cells go beyond making gas-exchange cells to repair damaged airways

abstract: The nation is on a trajectory to lead the world in science, a development that will reshape technological advancement, innovation and the balance of global power.
title: China’s extraordinary rise in science and how it will change the world

abstract: Explore China’s efforts to grow its scientific and technological might. Plus, how butterflies trick the eye and what could be the oldest shipwreck ever found.
title: Daily briefing: China’s extraordinary rise in science

abstract: Abstract Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition 1 . Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV–V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.
title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K

abstract: Abstract Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology 1,2 . Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes 1,3,4 . However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.
title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation

abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4–10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19. The AI framework probabilistic bias correction is shown to correct weather forecast errors 2 to 6 weeks ahead and boost forecast skill, making it promising for improved extreme-weather prediction.
title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning

title: Evidence for multi-Li+ clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes

abstract: Plastics have become an integral part of our modern society, largely because they are generally regarded as chemically inert under normal circumstances. However, plastics fragmented into microplastics (less than 5 mm in size) have recently raised significant public concerns, and have been detected widely across ecosystems and human tissues with increasing environmental and health risks1–5. Here we show that commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity in water, manifested by the spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species that increases with interfacial hydrophobicity and strongly correlates with interfacial electrostatics. Ab initio calculations support these observations and reveal that hydroxide oxidation becomes energetically more favourable at increasingly hydrophobic microplastic–water interfaces through the combined effects of partial solvation and electrostatics. These interfacial properties and the resulting oxidative chemistry have direct implications for biomolecular adsorption, protein aggregation, and even cellular damage. Together, our findings challenge the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, identify a possibly overlooked mechanism for the detrimental effects of microplastics on health and the environment, and contribute to a fundamental understanding of the structure–activity relationship of interfacial water, which may inform the design of safer and more sustainable plastic materials. Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment.
title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces

abstract: Astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas are isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas that most commonly arise in adults under the age of 50 and exhibit variable responses to treatment1–3. To understand the genetic drivers of disease progression, here we used whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing to characterize longitudinally collected tumour specimens from 183 patients with IDH-mutant glioma. Samples were collected through the Glioma Longitudinal Analysis (GLASS) Consortium4. Most primary surgery samples were classified as grade 2 on the basis of histology (73% for astrocytomas and 93% for oligodendrogliomas). We validated known genomic markers of tumour progression, including hypermutation and homozygous deletion of CDKN2A or CDKN2B (hereafter, CDKN2A/B)5, and discovered genetic alterations that distinguish between the evolutionary trajectories of astrocytomas and those of oligodendrogliomas. Mutations in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and NOTCH1 were newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas, regardless of treatment, and were associated with an increased tumour mutational burden. In recurrent astrocytomas, however, again irrespective of treatment, acquired focal oncogene amplifications and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions were associated with an increase in chromosomal imbalances, which converged with markers of chromosomal instability such as chromothripsis and whole-genome doubling. In both types of IDH-mutant glioma, we observed a convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse patient outcomes, suggesting that treatment-refractory clones were being selected. Treatment with temozolomide was associated with the mutational signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature increased in astrocytomas specifically. We show that the genomes of oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas adapt to the selective pressures of tumour progression and treatment in distinct ways, suggesting that oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas differ in their responses to treatment-induced DNA damage. Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.
title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas

abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1–7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In ‘low-dosage’ villages (in which 5–30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50–100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated–treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated–untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals’ connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable. A randomized controlled trial involving a health-education intervention in rural villages in Honduras shows that the intervention changed social network connections, including not only health-related connections but also friendships and financial ties.
title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks

abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). There are concerns that this potential near-doubling of conservation area coverage will negatively affect vulnerable people and over-stretch conservation resources4. However, nationally available datasets indicate that more conservation areas exist than are reflected in global figures5–7. We evaluated progress towards the area component of Target 3 using a globally representative sample across 25 countries and territories that incorporated these national datasets8. Extrapolating from this sample, we show that conservation areas likely already cover 26.81% of the terrestrial realm. We may be much closer to achieving 30% terrestrial coverage than previously thought. However, we also show that the extra land does not substantially address gaps in ecological representativeness, indicating that solely meeting the area component of Target 3 will do little to solve continuing global biodiversity loss. More focus and resources are needed to achieve the other components of the target, using a more strategic and inclusive approach to fill present gaps and produce equitable and effective conservation area networks. A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.
title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates

abstract: Abstract Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column 1–3 . During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle 4–6 , giving rise to a neck region. This head–shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats 4,5,7–9 . However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components 10 have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head–shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by Eusthenopteron ) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head–shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods 11–14 , provides a better functional explanation for the head–shoulder separation.
title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue

abstract: Abstract The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis 1–5 . Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential 6–10 . Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.
title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics

abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans. Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.
title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat

abstract: Abstract Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities 1–5 . Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.
title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism

abstract: To the Editor:Dengue, a significant global health threat, currently lacks effective antiviral treatments. 1 Mosnodenvir is an antiviral against dengue virus (DENV) infection which has reached phase 2 clinical development in a prophylactic setting. 2 Initial results from this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a trial (Cohort 1[C1]) have been published 1 and were expanded with additional daily (QD) and weekly (Q7D) dose regimens in Cohort 2 (C2).Loading doses (LD) started on Day (D) -2 twice daily (BID) for 2 days, followed by maintenance doses (MD) as QD or Q7D for 21 days (QD, 800 mg/250 mg, Q7D high-dose 450 mg/1200 mg and low-dose 250 mg/500 mg).The under-attenuated virus rDEN3Δ30 was subcutaneously injected on D1 with safety, pharmacokinetics, virology and serology parameters evaluated up to D120 (Figure 1A).The protocol and Supplementary Appendix are available with the full text of this letter at NEJM.org.
title: Once-Weekly Mosnodenvir as Dengue Prophylaxis in a Human Infection Model

abstract: BACKGROUND: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges. METHODS: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point. RESULTS: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2). CONCLUSIONS: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).
title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges

abstract: BACKGROUND: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection. METHODS: We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Participants were assigned to receive icotrokinra at a once-daily dose of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 100 mg or placebo. The primary end point was clinical response at week 12. Secondary end points included clinical remission, remission of symptoms, and endoscopic improvement at week 12. RESULTS: A total of 252 participants underwent randomization: 63 were assigned to the 400-mg group, 62 to the 200-mg group, 64 to the 100-mg group, and 63 to the placebo group. All the doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo with respect to a clinical response at week 12, which occurred in 63% of the participants in the 400-mg group, 58% in the 200-mg group, and 55% in the 100-mg group, as compared with 27% in the placebo group (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants with clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher in the 400-mg group than in the placebo group (30% vs. 11%, P = 0.006), as were the percentage of participants with symptomatic remission (46% vs. 19%, P<0.001) and the percentage of participants with endoscopic improvement (37% vs. 14%, P = 0.002). Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 24% of the participants in the 200-mg group (P = 0.054 for the comparison with placebo); in accordance with the fixed-sequence testing procedure to account for multiple comparisons, no further formal testing of secondary end points was conducted. Through week 28, the percentage of participants with adverse events was 60% in the 400-mg group, 66% in the 200-mg group, 66% in the 100-mg group, and 62% in the placebo group. For serious adverse events, the percentages were 2%, 5%, 0%, and 10%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, a clinical response at week 12 was significantly more common with once-daily oral icotrokinra at each of three tested doses than with placebo. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; ANTHEM-UC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06049017.).
title: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis

abstract: BACKGROUND: The outcome of Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-positive ALL) has greatly improved with the use of tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immunotherapy. METHODS: In this trial, we randomly assigned adult patients with Ph-positive ALL in a 2:1 ratio to receive ponatinib plus blinatumomab (intervention group) or imatinib plus chemotherapy (control group) as frontline treatment. A crossover to the intervention group was allowed for patients with persistence or reappearance of measurable residual disease in the control group. The primary end point was event-free survival. RESULTS: A total of 236 patients underwent randomization: 158 to the intervention group and 78 to the control group. The median age of the patients was 55 years (range, 24 to 82). At a median follow-up of 23.7 months, the estimated 24-month event-free survival was 86% in the intervention group and 67% in the control group (P<0.001). Survival with no measurable residual disease was 68% and 42%, respectively. At the end of induction, a complete hematologic response was observed in 94% of the patients in the intervention group and in 79% of those in the control group. After blinatumomab consolidation, a molecular response was observed in 71% and 49% of the patients, respectively. After crossover to the intervention group, 20 of 31 patients (64%) had a molecular response. Overall survival was 90% in the intervention group and 85% in the control group. The cumulative incidence of relapse was 5% and 13%, respectively. As of this report, only 19% of the patients in the intervention group had undergone hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after having had a first complete hematologic response. CONCLUSIONS: In this phase 3 trial, a frontline chemotherapy-free targeted and immunotherapeutic approach was superior to the use of imatinib and chemotherapy. (Funded by Associazione Italiana per la Ricerca sul Cancro and others; GIMEMA ALL2820 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04722848.).
title: Ponatinib–Blinatumomab or Imatinib–Chemotherapy for Adult Ph-Positive ALL

abstract: BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group. CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).
title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury

abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).
title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non–Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes

abstract: Limited selenium (Se) accumulation in agricultural products contributes to widespread dietary Se deficiency, posing a global nutritional threat. Efficient agronomic strategies to enhance Se biofortification in crops are still lacking. Here, we reveal the synergistic effects of shading and Se nanoparticles application on Se biofortification in tea leaves. Field experiments demonstrate that shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves under sufficient Se supply, through activating Se metabolism pathway. We identify CsAPR1 functions at the early stage of Se assimilation, catalyzing the reduction of Se (VI). The transcription of CsAPR1 is activated by CsMYB7-like and is further promoted by shading through interaction with CsbHLH70. Under sunlight, CsHY5 competes with CsbHLH70 for binding to CsMYB7-like, thereby attenuating CsMYB7-like-mediated transcription of CsAPR1 and suppressing Se accumulation in tea plants. Our findings reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying shade-induced enhancement of Se biofortification, offering insights and strategies for Se-enriched crop production.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves through promoting CsMYB7-like-mediated conversion of Se (VI) to Se (IV)

abstract: While fivefold point symmetry is common in nature, fivefold spatial symmetry is seldom observed. Regular pentagons cannot tile a plane without leaving voids, and even the densest “ice-ray” packing is exceptionally rare. Fivefold helices are equally elusive. We report a small molecule that self-assembles into hydrogen-bonded pseudo-fivefold helices and adopts an ice-ray pentagonal packing motif over crystallographic length scales using peripheral disorder that partially occupies regions that would otherwise be void in an ideal pentagonal tessellation. The resulting structure exhibits weak and nondirectional interhelical interactions within the ( bc ) plane and comparatively strong and directional intrahelical hydrogen bonding along the a axis. This structural anisotropy gives rise to single crystals with large aspect ratios and distinct mechanical behavior. This realization of two rare structural motifs within a single crystal shows the capability of simple organic molecules to form complex structures and highlights an untapped potential for symmetry engineering in molecular solids through the interplay of intermolecular interactions with pronounced differences in strength and directionality.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Ice-ray pentagonal packing of pseudo-fivefold helices

abstract: Miniaturization, the reduction of adult body size to an extreme degree, has evolved repeatedly across vertebrates. Yet its genomic underpinnings remain poorly understood. Cypriniformes, the most species-rich order of freshwater fishes, contains multiple miniaturized lineages that have evolved via contrasting developmental processes. Proportioned dwarfs are tiny-bodied but otherwise morphologically similar to larger relatives, while progenetic miniatures exhibit developmental truncation and retain larval-like anatomical features into adulthood. Using a new time-calibrated phylogeny of 309 cypriniform species and comparative genomic analyses of 33 high-quality genome assemblies, we investigated the evolutionary history and genomic correlates of miniaturization across this order. Ancestral state reconstruction revealed multiple independent origins of both miniature types, with reversals to the nonminiature state rarely recovered and miniature origins nonrandomly distributed across the phylogeny. The origins of the two types of miniatures differed in their timing. Progenetic miniatures arose predominantly in the Eocene whereas proportioned dwarfs arose mainly within the Miocene period. Genome size variation across Cypriniformes has been overwhelmingly driven by polyploidy. However, progenetic miniatures showed a directionally consistent, though nonsignificant, trend toward genome size reduction. Comparative genomic analyses revealed that all three independently evolved progenetic miniature lineages share convergent signatures of repeat loss alongside genome-wide intron shortening, patterns absent in proportioned dwarfs. Our study provides the broadest evidence to date that progenetic miniaturization, despite independent origins, is underpinned by predictable structural genomic changes, revealing a fundamental link between developmental truncation and genome architecture in vertebrates.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Convergent genome streamlining accompanies independent miniaturization in the world’s smallest fishes

abstract: Methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 3 (MBD3), an essential component of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex, controls chromatin accessibility at lineage-specific transcriptional enhancers and promoters during hematopoietic cell differentiation. Here, we have shown that MBD3 deficiency in the T cell compartment resulted in spontaneous development of T cell–mediated multiorgan autoimmune diseases including fatal autoimmune myocarditis. The MBD3-deficient mice notably showed a significant reduction of CD25 + Foxp3 + regulatory T (Treg) cells in both the thymus and periphery without much affecting the development and function of conventional T (Tconv) cells. Mixed bone marrow (BM) chimeras reconstituted with wild-type and MBD3-deficient BM revealed a cell-intrinsic defect in thymic Treg cell lineage differentiation in MBD3-deficient cells. Transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional analyses of thymocyte subsets further revealed that MBD3 deficiency particularly affected the activation of a Treg-specific enhancer of the Il2ra gene encoding CD25, hence impaired CD25 expression in immature CD4 single-positive thymocytes (ImCD4SP) but not in peripheral T cells. The impairment markedly limited thymic Treg precursor cell generation and substantially reduced overall thymic Treg cell output. By contrast, MBD3 deficiency scarcely impacted the TGF-β/IL-2-dependent in vitro Treg cell generation from Tconv cells. Thus, Treg-specific developmental properties such as high IL-2/CD25 dependency of their thymic differentiation may render them more sensitive than Tconv cells to epigenetic changes of the whole T cell compartment. The results provide a mechanistic basis by which general epigenomic alterations in the T cell compartment can be causative of autoimmune and other immunological diseases through selectively affecting thymic Treg cell development.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Autoimmunity induced by epigenome alteration affecting thymic Treg cell development

abstract: While complex-pole hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) have dramatically expanded the reach of numerically exact quantum dynamics simulations of open quantum systems, they suffer from numerical instabilities rooted in the non-Hermitian structure of their Liouvillian. Yet, the origin of this structure remains obscure. Here, we report a previously unknown gauge freedom in complex-pole HEOM: a continuous family of analytically equivalent Liouvillians, all encoding the same bath correlation function, whose numerical properties vary dramatically. This gauge controls both the eigenspectrum and non-normality of the hierarchy generator, revealing spectral divergence and non-normal error amplification as two distinct instability mechanisms. By optimizing this gauge, we introduce GO--HEOM, which eliminates divergences in strongly coupled Brownian oscillator environments and extends numerically exact simulations of sub-Ohmic dynamics -- including through the delocalized-to-localized quantum phase transition -- to previously inaccessible coupling strengths. Because this gauge transformation is independent of the bath-correlation decomposition scheme, our GO--HEOM becomes a general, broadly compatible strategy for accessing numerically exact quantum dynamics of open quantum systems over arbitrary coupling and highly non-Markovian regimes.
title: Hidden gauge freedom in complex-pole hierarchical equations of motion

abstract: The nonlinear Hall effect in quantum materials has attracted broad interest, yet most existing studies focus on the weak-field, perturbative regime. Here we develop a nonperturbative approach based on nonequilibrium steady-state Green's functions for dc-field-driven lattice systems, with dissipation and interactions incorporated through self-energies beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation and interband transitions treated alongside their intraband counterparts. Applied to a two-band semimetal model, our approach provides direct access to the strong-field Hall response beyond the nonperturbative crossover where the edge of the nonequilibrium distribution reaches Berry-curvature hot spots, a regime in which constant relaxation-time estimates and Berry curvature dipole calculations become unreliable. We further demonstrate that interaction and electron-phonon self-energies within dynamical mean-field theory can substantially change the Hall signal. Our framework enables quantitative simulations of nonequilibrium nonlinear Hall phenomena and provides guidance for strong-field transport experiments.
title: Nonperturbative nonlinear Hall effect in nonequilibrium steady states

abstract: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties. Furthermore, we extend our investigation to two-dimensional QWs, where a single non-Hermitian defect also induces scale-free localization, thereby demonstrating the universality of this phenomenon. Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.
title: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk

abstract: Freshwater scarcity demands desalination technologies that are efficient, scalable, and sustainable. Capacitive deionisation (CDI) is promising but remains limited by inefficient ion adsorption and poor charge utilisation. Here, we show that suitably chosen polyampholytic block copolymer grafting can substantially enhance CDI performance, via a combination of dipolar response and steric effects. Using mean-field classical density functional theory and grand-canonical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that such polymer grafted electrodes enable strongly improved desalination performance, without altering the pore architecture. Even an electrode grafting by simple neutral polymers can generate an improvement, although a suitably designed block polymer architecture offers an additional performance gain. These results establish interfacial block copolymer grafting as a powerful route toward high-performance, membrane-free desalination.
title: Improved desalination by polymer grafting
